headline: Neighbours who meet — Homebody gets its first third-party bond
lede: Every bond in HOMEBODY pointed back to the household. Fern and Ivy now form an opinion of their own: shared afternoons climb a NEIGH bond of their own, and friends on speaking terms chat deeper with the house. The social web finally has a spoke the player's house isn't on.

notes.text: rel.neigh (#2588, live): two free neighbours chat at 0.05/s within ring 2; a waiting one glances across at 0.02/s; idle and apart, Ivy crosses the room while Fern keeps house etiquette — and neither drifts back to the furniture while they're together.

Cross-warmth: at rung 1+, each neighbour's chat with the household runs 25% deeper — friend of my friend, byte-identical below the rung. Twin-leaf NEIGH row on the BONDS panel; marquee teaches the law.

peoplecheck 722/722 (+26 gates), two named mutants die; homebodydrive 92/92 with the four-row phone-scale BONDS leg. The #2579 claim went to slot b on a fresh checkpoint; the never-dry ladder picked Homebody (score 2) and it shipped.
Polish pass filed as #2599: pair-hued bubbles, a wave beat on the meet-up, attract-window overlap, a warmth sparkle.
